newsitem.title: USA: First Merchants Acceptance faces lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: First Merchants Acceptance faces lawsuit.

text.p: First Merchants Acceptance Corp faces a lawsuit a week after it announced having discovered irregularities in its financial records.
A law firm said Tuesday it had filed a suit against the company in the District Court for the Northern District of Illinois for alleged securities fraud.
The suit is the latest in a series filed against the company in the last week.
The firm, Bernstein Litowitz Berger & Grossmann LLP, said it filed the suit on behalf of a group of investors who bought the stock between April 18, 1996, and April 17, 1997.

On April 16, the company said it would have to restate its net income for the 1996 fiscal year ended December 31, 1996, from $1.56 a share to $1.00 due "accounting irregularities" discovered in its books.

It said corporate insiders made unauthorized entries in its financial records that disguised the true extent to which it maintained non-performing or under-performing loans in its portfolio as current and performing.
The company, which dismissed its chief executive officer and three other employees, has since see its stock fall to a year low of 2-1/2 on the Nasdaq.
Although company officials were not immediately available for comment, a spokeswoman contacted by Reuters on Monday declined to comment on another suit filed against it.
